newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.3 percent in October.
newsitem.headline: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.3 percent in October.

text.p: Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, rose 0.3 percent in October after rising a revised 0.2 percent (0.1 percent) in September, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
Note: GDP figures are in billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates at factor cost, constant 1986 dollars.

The strong 0.3 percent increase in GDP for the month occurred despite a long strike in the motor vehicle industry. Excluding manufacturers of motor vehicles and parts, GDP advanced 0.6 percent. The rest of manufacturing, wholesale trade, finance and related services and the mining sector led the advance, the government agency said.
Manufacturing production fell 0.6 percent in October although output increased in 16 of 21 major groups.
Manufacturing output actually rose 1.0 percent excluding motor vehicles and parts, it said.
Wholesaling activity rose 1.9 percent. Sales increased rapidly in most trade groups, led by computers and software packages, motor vehicles and parts and construction materials.
Retailing advanced 0.6 percent in october, its fourth gain in five months as consumer demand showed some signs of awakening, it said. Sales in supermarkets and by auto dealers led the increase.
